draft.title: Democracy in Athens
card: Democracy means rule by the people. Athens was a democracy about 2,500 years ago, in the 5th century BCE.
Citizens met in a body called the Assembly. They voted directly on laws and on matters such as war. They did not elect people to vote for them.
Only free adult men born to Athenian parents were citizens.
Women, slaves and foreigners were not citizens, so they had no vote. Most people living in Athens could not take part.
draft.remember: Athenian democracy gave citizens a direct vote, but only a small group counted as citizens.

a.q: Which person could vote on laws in the Athenian Assembly?
opts: A free man whose parents were both Athenian
A free woman whose parents were both Athenian
A foreign man who had lived in Athens for years
A man who was enslaved and worked in Athens
a.why: Only free adult men born to Athenian parents were citizens, and only citizens could vote. The foreign man lived in Athens, but living there did not make him a citizen.
a.clue: Think about who counted as a citizen.

b.q: Athens is often called a democracy. Why is it fair to say that its democracy was limited?
opts: Most people living in Athens were not citizens
Citizens did not vote on laws themselves
Citizens only voted on matters of war
The Assembly did not let citizens speak
b.why: Women, slaves and foreigners were not citizens, so most people in Athens had no vote. Citizens did vote directly on laws, so the other options describe things that did not happen.
b.clue: Count who was left out, not how citizens voted.

a.best: A free man whose parents were both Athenian

b.best: Most people living in Athens were not citizens

problems.detail: The clue 'Count who was left out, not how citizens voted' rules out every distractor, since each is about how citizens voted or took part. A student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are correct. The clue for question b gives the answer away by ruling out all three wrong options.

b.q: Athens is often called a democracy. Why is it fair to say that its democracy was limited?
opts: Most people living in Athens were not citizens
Citizens elected others to vote on laws for them
Women could vote, but slaves and foreigners could not
Citizens could vote only on matters of war
b.why: Women, slaves and foreigners were not citizens, so most people in Athens had no vote. Women were left out too, so the option saying they could vote is wrong. Citizens voted directly on laws as well as war, so the other two options did not happen.
b.clue: Recall which groups were not citizens.
